results.answer:
The FAA issues Airworthiness Directives that apply to the Boeing 737 MAX. For the LEAP-1B engine mount the relevant chain is:

1. **FAA AD 2024-01-02** - issued under 49 USC 106(g), 40113, 44701 and **applies to** the Boeing 737 MAX (graph relationship). It **supersedes** earlier AD 2020-05-11 and AD 2022-03-07.  
2. Boeing, as the Design Approval Holder, incorporates the requirements of that AD into its **Component Maintenance Manual for the engine mount (737MAX_CMM_Engine_Mount)**.  
3. **Revision 12** of the CMM (dated Nov 2023) states that inspection intervals were **updated per FAA AD 2024-01-02 compliance**. The manual (Section 71-21-05, Chapter 71 - Power Plant) provides the specific inspection and maintenance actions for the CFM LEAP-1B engine mount.  
4. The **maintenance crew** follows the procedures and intervals described in that CMM revision when performing inspections or maintenance on the LEAP-1B engine mount.

Thus the regulatory path is: **FAA → AD 2024-01-02 (and superseded ADs) → Boeing’s updated CMM (rev 12) → maintenance crew**.

results.answer:
Southwest’s 737 MAX MCAS compliance timeline  

* **Grounding & return-to-service** - All 737-8/9 aircraft were grounded by the FAA Emergency Order on 13 Mar 2019 (Chunk 481f850c). Southwest’s first MAX 8 entered service on 29 Aug 2017, was grounded with the fleet, and returned to revenue service on 11 Mar 2021 (Chunk 51dc0547).  

* **FAA AD 2020-05-11** - Required MCAS Software v1.7.2 (released May 2020). Southwest met this AD; the fleet was “COMPLIANT - all 87 aircraft (pre-service compliance Nov 2020)” (Chunk 766333cc).  

* **FAA AD 2022-03-07** - Added enhanced AOA-monitoring requirements. Southwest complied with this AD as well (“COMPLIANT - all 87 aircraft (completed Apr 2022)”) (Chunk 766333cc).  

* **FAA AD 2024-01-02** - Requires installation of MCAS Software v2.0 or later (supersedes AD 2020-05-11 and AD 2022-03-07 per the known graph). The compliance deadline is 15 May 2024 (Chunk b7a99dea; Chunk 766333cc).  

* **Current fleet status (Jan 2024)** - Southwest operates 87 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft, each running MCAS v1.7.3 (Chunk 1f57a50e). This version satisfies the earlier ADs but not AD 2024-01-02, so the fleet is “IS_NON_COMPLIANT_WITH” the new requirement, though the deadline has not yet passed (Chunk b7a99dea).  

* **Planned compliance actions** - Software updates are scheduled February-May 2024, phased at roughly 10 aircraft per month, using Boeing Service Bulletin [SSN_REDACTED] Rev 2 (3.5 h estimated) during the April 22-23 2024 D-check slot (Chunk b7a99dea). The target is MCAS v2.0 on all 87 aircraft before the 15 May 2024 deadline.  

* **Regulatory consequence** - Under 14 CFR Part 39, non-compliance after the deadline would render the aircraft unairworthy (Chunk 5c67bf85).  

**Summary:** Southwest complied with the 2020 and 2022 MCAS-related ADs, but as of early 2024 its 737 MAX fleet still runs MCAS v1.7.3, making it non-compliant with AD 2024-01-02. The airline has a phased upgrade plan to install MCAS v2.0 on all 87 MAX 8s by the 15 May 2024 deadline, after which the fleet will be fully compliant.
